episode.title: Adapt provider configuration and request routing for alternate hosted endpoints
episode.before: At first parent ec658223692f901c7456d5baa426e5a8d696dfb7, the command interface accepted only an API key and base URL. Coder.create required those values, assigned them to the provider SDK, and every chat-completion request contained the common model/messages/temperature/stream fields but no deployment_id or engine routing fields. This coupled provider initialization to coder construction and could not express the additional endpoint type, API version, deployment, and engine settings required by alternate hosted interfaces.
episode.after: At merge commit 549a1a76403e309890410f9538bda2fc4f901758, startup accepts optional base, type, version, deployment ID, and engine settings, maps each supplied value to the corresponding provider SDK module attribute, and initializes the API key before constructing the coder. Coder.create no longer owns provider credentials or endpoint configuration. At the request boundary, deployment_id and engine are conditionally copied from SDK module attributes into ChatCompletion.create keyword arguments. Documentation provides command-line and configuration-file examples. Tests were adjusted to the new Coder.create interface, although no provider-specific behavioral test was added and one benchmark call site still uses the removed positional API-key argument.
episode.diff: Compared with first parent ec658223692f901c7456d5baa426e5a8d696dfb7, the merge changes seven files (95 insertions, 46 deletions): aider/main.py adds four advanced provider options and centralizes SDK configuration; aider/coders/base_coder.py removes provider setup from Coder.create and conditionally forwards deployment/engine routing fields; docs/faq.md documents alternate-hosted endpoint configuration; and four test modules remove obsolete API-key arguments from Coder.create calls. Static call-site inspection also finds benchmark/benchmark.py was not reconciled and still passes an extra positional API-key value.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned ref 549a1a76403e309890410f9538bda2fc4f901758 is the merge for pull request 88, has first parent ec658223692f901c7456d5baa426e5a8d696dfb7, and describes adding arguments to configure the provider module for an alternate hosted service.

Before the change, the advanced model interface exposed only --openai-api-base with a fixed default, while Coder.create required openai_api_key and optionally openai_api_base and directly assigned both SDK module attributes.

candidate_atomics.name: configure-provider-client-at-startup
candidate_atomics.description: Accept optional provider-interface settings at the application boundary and apply supplied values to the shared SDK client before constructing downstream workers.

semantic_action.intent: Allow a compatible but differently hosted provider interface to supply endpoint, protocol-version, and routing configuration without hard-coding a single default endpoint.
semantic_action.module_role: application startup and provider-client configuration boundary
semantic_action.pre_state: Startup can supply only a credential and base URL, and provider SDK initialization occurs inside worker construction.
semantic_action.post_state: Startup maps each supplied provider setting to the SDK client before worker construction while leaving unspecified optional settings untouched.
semantic_action.validation: Main-entry tests provide a regression oracle for startup and worker creation, while the documented command/YAML examples specify the intended configuration contract; no direct assertions for every new mapping were added.

candidate_atomics.name: decouple-worker-construction-from-provider-initialization
candidate_atomics.description: Remove provider credentials and endpoint mutation from the worker factory so provider lifecycle configuration has a single startup owner.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent worker construction from owning or overwriting global provider-client configuration.
semantic_action.module_role: worker factory and lifecycle ownership boundary
semantic_action.pre_state: The worker factory requires provider credentials and assigns global SDK key and base attributes during every construction.
semantic_action.post_state: The worker factory selects and creates worker implementations without accepting or mutating provider configuration.
semantic_action.validation: Updated coder, command, and editing tests instantiate workers through the reduced interface; static call-site inspection exposes one unreconciled benchmark invocation.

candidate_atomics.name: adapt-request-routing-fields-at-provider-call
candidate_atomics.description: Conditionally translate configured deployment and engine selectors into request-level arguments at the external completion-call boundary.

semantic_action.intent: Route completion requests through provider interfaces that require deployment or engine selectors in addition to a model name.
semantic_action.pre_state: Completion requests include model, messages, temperature, streaming, and optional function data but never include configured deployment or engine selectors.
semantic_action.post_state: When deployment or engine attributes are present on the configured SDK client, the request forwards them as deployment_id and engine; otherwise the existing request shape is retained.
semantic_action.validation: The implementation constructs the final keyword map immediately before ChatCompletion.create, but the changed test suite contains no provider-specific assertion of these conditional fields.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt-a-client-to-an-alternate-compatible-provider-interface
candidate_workflows.description: Centralize optional provider configuration at startup, remove that responsibility from downstream worker construction, and forward request-only routing selectors at the external API boundary while preserving the ordinary request shape when selectors are absent.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow the application to use a compatible provider interface with additional endpoint and routing requirements without coupling provider state to worker construction.
workflow_graph.entry_state: The application supports a credential and base URL, initializes provider state inside the worker factory, and cannot forward deployment or engine selectors on completion requests.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Supplied provider settings are established once at startup, worker construction is provider-configuration agnostic, and configured request-routing selectors reach the external completion call while absent selectors do not change its ordinary shape.
unresolved_or_deferred: No changed test directly verifies mapping of base/type/version/deployment/engine values onto the SDK client.
No changed test asserts that deployment_id or engine is present or absent in the final completion request.
Runtime test execution was unavailable because pytest is not installed in the extraction environment.
The benchmark invocation was not updated to the reduced Coder.create signature and would need reconciliation before claiming all call sites are valid.
Live connectivity to an alternate hosted endpoint is not established by repository evidence.

unresolved_questions: Did pull request 88 have external CI or live endpoint validation? The GitHub bundle contains no status checks, reviews, or discussion metadata.
Was benchmark/benchmark.py intentionally excluded from the constructor migration, or is its remaining positional API-key argument an overlooked incompatibility?
The implementation checks attribute existence rather than a non-None routing value at request time; repository tests do not establish behavior if those SDK attributes already exist with null values.
